script: Good morning, this is Stocksplain for Tuesday, November 24. The biggest story today is the dramatic return of Jensen Huang to the helm of Nvidia. After resigning just eleven days ago amid personal scandals and national security concerns, the board has unanimously voted to reinstate him as chief executive officer. The news triggered a massive market rally, with Nvidia shares jumping thirty percent in a single day, adding nearly one trillion dollars in market value. The move followed intense pressure from shareholders and a direct phone call from President Trump. While the market is celebrating, the situation highlights the deep reliance of the entire tech sector on a single visionary leader. In other major news, the cybersecurity industry is seeing a massive consolidation. CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at forty-four billion dollars. This move is part of a broader race to integrate artificial intelligence into digital defenses against increasingly sophisticated threats. Meanwhile, in the pharmaceutical sector, Sanofi is making a major play for growth, agreeing to buy the biotech firm Insmed for forty-one billion dollars. This is the largest deal in the industry in three years, aimed at expanding their pipeline for rare diseases. Finally, on the economic front, a survey from the National Association for Business Economics shows that eighty-two percent of businesses are reporting rising material costs. This is the highest level since nineteen ninety-nine, driven by factors like energy prices, tariffs, and high interest rates. This suggests that inflationary pressures may remain a persistent challenge for companies and consumers alike. Today's concept is key-person risk. This term describes the vulnerability a company faces when its success, investor trust, and valuation are heavily concentrated in one individual. When that leader faces personal scandal or leaves, the firm can suffer sudden, extreme losses in market value. We saw this play out in real time with Nvidia. When Huang resigned, the company lost hundreds of billions in value, but his return sparked a massive rebound. This dependency is a double-edged sword for investors. While a strong leader can drive incredible growth, their personal risks become the company's risks. To mitigate this, Nvidia's board is now adding a new chairman and a national security committee to provide better oversight. Understanding this risk is essential for any investor looking at high-growth tech stocks. Thanks for listening, and we will see you tomorrow.
